option_description: Whether Office VBA macros originating from the internet are blocked by policy (macro-block GPO / Defender ASR) so a phishing attachment cannot auto-execute a macro on open.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of the exposure "Phishing-driven user execution (initial access)" — fires when macros are enabled by default (office_macro_execution_blocked false) and a malicious attachment can run a macro on open (ATT&CK T1204/T1059).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the PowerShell execution policy (the macro/script policy surface) and confirm the macro-block GPO/Defender ASR rule for internet-sourced Office documents is deployed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Machine/CurrentUser policy AllSigned or RemoteSigned with a macro-block GPO in place (secure); Unrestricted/Bypass or no macro-block policy (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 10 — Malware Defenses

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the GPO/Intune setting 'Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet' (or the equivalent ASR rule GUID) is enforced for the Office apps in scope.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Group Policy / Intune: Office macro settings — 'Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet' set to Enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Internet-sourced macros blocked by policy (secure); macros allowed/enabled by default (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether script/command-interpreter execution is constrained (PowerShell Constrained Language mode plus AllSigned/RemoteSigned execution policy, signed-only scripts), cutting the phishing-to-execution path via PowerShell/VBA/shell.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of the exposure "Phishing-driven user execution (initial access)" — fires when interpreters can run arbitrary unsigned payloads (script_execution_constrained false), enabling ATT&CK T1059 command/scripting abuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List the effective PowerShell execution policy at each scope on the macro/script policy surface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Machine/CurrentUser policy AllSigned or RemoteSigned (secure); Unrestricted/Bypass (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 10 — Malware Defenses

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm PowerShell runs in Constrained Language mode (typically enforced by WDAC/AppLocker).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ConstrainedLanguage (secure); FullLanguage with no allowlisting (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether application/script allowlisting is enforced (WDAC/AppLocker on Windows; Gatekeeper assessments on macOS) so only approved, signed binaries may execute, blocking unsigned/unknown phishing payloads.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of the exposure "Phishing-driven user execution (initial access)" — fires when any downloaded binary may run (application_allowlisting_enforced false), the on-host execution step of ATT&CK T1204.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On macOS check Gatekeeper assessment state; on Windows confirm a WDAC/AppLocker policy is deployed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: macOS: "assessments enabled" (Gatekeeper on, secure); "assessments disabled" (insecure). Windows: confirm WDAC/AppLocker policy deployed.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 2 — Inventory and Control of Software Assets; Control 10

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, enumerate effective AppLocker policy to confirm allowlisting rules are present and enforcing.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enforcing rule collections for Exe/Script/Msi (secure); no policy or AuditOnly (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether protective DNS plus web/email content filtering is active on the endpoint to block known-malicious domains and phishing-payload download/callback.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of the exposure "Phishing-driven user execution (initial access)" — fires when arbitrary domains are resolvable and no web/email filtering blocks the lure (web_dns_content_filtering_enabled false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the endpoint resolves through protective DNS and that web/email content-filtering policy is applied.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Endpoint resolves via protective DNS and web filtering policy is applied (secure); unfiltered resolution (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 9/13 — content filtering and network monitoring

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to resolve a known test/blocked malicious domain from the endpoint to confirm protective DNS sinkholes it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Resolution blocked/sinkholed by protective DNS (secure); domain resolves normally (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether EDR/AV behavior-based monitoring is active on the endpoint so post-click payload execution and fileless/behavior-only malware are detected and blocked.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of both "Phishing-driven user execution (initial access)" and "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" — fires when behavior monitoring is off (behavior_monitoring_enabled false) and a payload executes undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Defender antimalware status object and inspect BehaviorMonitorEnabled (or the equivalent EDR console flag).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BehaviorMonitorEnabled : True (secure); False indicates behavior monitoring is disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Get-MpComputerStatus (Defender) Microsoft Learn

option_description: Endpoint anti-malware (EDR/AV) is installed and its service is running (Get-MpComputerStatus AMServiceEnabled and AntivirusEnabled both True). The core malware-defense control on the endpoint.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" — fires when the core malware-defense control is absent (edr_av_present false) and malware executes unimpeded.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Defender antimalware status object and confirm the service is enabled and antivirus is active (or that the EDR sensor service is installed and running).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AMServiceEnabled : True and AntivirusEnabled : True (secure); either False indicates the agent is absent/disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Get-MpComputerStatus (Defender) Microsoft Learn

option_description: Real-time / on-access scanning is active (Get-MpComputerStatus RealTimeProtectionEnabled and OnAccessProtectionEnabled True) so files are inspected on access and boot/logon autostart persistence is observed.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of both "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" and "Boot-level persistence / firmware bootkit" — fires when real-time protection is off (realtime_protection_enabled false), so files execute without on-access inspection and persistence goes unmonitored.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Defender antimalware status object and inspect RealTimeProtectionEnabled and OnAccessProtectionEnabled (or the equivalent EDR flag).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RealTimeProtectionEnabled : True and OnAccessProtectionEnabled : True (secure); either False indicates real-time protection is disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Get-MpComputerStatus (Defender) Microsoft Learn

option_description: Tamper protection prevents malware or a local actor from disabling AV/EDR or altering its settings (Get-MpComputerStatus IsTamperProtected True).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" — fires when tamper protection is off (edr_tamper_protection_enabled false), letting an Impair-Defenses actor (ATT&CK T1562) silently disable the agent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Defender antimalware status object and inspect IsTamperProtected (or the EDR console tamper-protection toggle).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IsTamperProtected : True (secure) — protection settings cannot be silently disabled; False (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Protect security settings with tamper protection — Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Learn

option_description: Age in days of the anti-malware signature/definition package (Get-MpComputerStatus AntivirusSignatureAge). Stale signatures miss known threats.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" — fires when above the freshness threshold (>3 days), because stale signatures miss known threats; secure endpoints sit at or near 0.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Defender signature-currency fields (or the EDR last-definition-update timestamp converted to days).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AntivirusSignatureAge near 0 with a recent AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated timestamp (secure); a large age value (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Get-MpComputerStatus (Defender) Microsoft Learn

option_description: Removable-media device control restricts USB mass-storage write/execute via policy.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Malware execution with disabled or stale endpoint protection" — fires when device control is off (removable_media_control_enabled false), letting removable media seed a malware payload (ATT&CK T1091 Replication Through Removable Media).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a deployed MDM/GPO device-control policy restricts removable-storage read/write/execute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MDM/GPO device-control policy restricts removable storage (secure); no policy / full access (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 10 — Malware Defenses (auto-run/removable media); Control 13

option_description: True when the OS and third-party client software (browser, document readers) have no missing critical/important security updates per the org patch SLA.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Exploitation of unpatched OS / third-party client software" — fires when patches are missing (os_patch_current false), leaving known-vulnerable client software exploitable via web or document content (ATT&CK T1203).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List the most recently installed hotfixes/cumulative updates and cross-check the latest InstalledOn date against the vendor patch SLA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A recent InstalledOn date for the latest cumulative update (secure); a months-old last patch (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 / Control 2 — patch and software currency

option_description: True when automatic OS and software updates are enabled so security fixes install without manual intervention within the SLA window.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Exploitation of unpatched OS / third-party client software" — fires when auto-update is disabled (automatic_updates_enabled false), since the endpoint drifts out of date and remains exploitable (ATT&CK T1203).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm patches are being applied automatically by inspecting recent install cadence; cross-check the OS/MDM auto-update policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Regular recent InstalledOn dates indicating auto-update applies fixes within SLA (secure); stale cadence (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 / Control 2 — patch and software currency

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the Windows Update / MDM update policy (or package-manager auto-update) is set to install OS and managed third-party security updates automatically.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Auto-update policy enabled for OS and managed software (secure); manual/disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Number of days since the most recent security patch / cumulative update was installed (latest InstalledOn date via Get-HotFix or equivalent).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Exploitation of unpatched OS / third-party client software" — fires when it exceeds 30 days, indicating the patch SLA has lapsed (ATT&CK T1203); a hardened endpoint stays near 0.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Find the latest InstalledOn date and compute days between today and that date (or use the OS/software last-update timestamp).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A recent latest InstalledOn date yielding a small day count (secure); a months-old date yielding >30 days (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 / Control 2 — patch and software currency

option_description: Windows Defender Credential Guard is running (Win32_DeviceGuard SecurityServicesRunning includes 1), isolating LSASS-derived secrets (NTLM hashes, Kerberos TGTs, cached domain credentials) in a VBS-protected container.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Local credential theft and reuse" — fires when Credential Guard is off (credential_guard_enabled false) and LSASS secrets are harvestable for reuse (ATT&CK T1552 Unsecured Credentials).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Win32_DeviceGuard and inspect which security services are actually running.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SecurityServicesRunning includes 1 (Credential Guard running) (secure); empty/0 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6; MITRE ATT&CK T1552 Unsecured Credentials (mitigation)

option_description: LSA protection (RunAsPPL — LSASS runs as a Protected Process Light) is enabled, blocking unprivileged/userland tools from opening LSASS to dump credential material.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Local credential theft and reuse" — fires when LSASS is unprotected (lsa_protection_enabled false) and credential-dumping tooling can read secrets directly (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the LSA RunAsPPL registry value to confirm LSASS runs as a Protected Process Light.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RunAsPPL = 1 (or 2 for UEFI-locked) (secure); missing or 0 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the RunAsPPL setting is enforced via GPO/Intune across the fleet, not just set locally.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RunAsPPL enforced centrally (secure); unmanaged / not configured (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Interactive day-to-day user accounts are standard users and the local Administrators group is limited to authorized admin accounts (least privilege, NIST AC-6).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Local credential theft and reuse" — fires when the everyday user holds local admin rights (endpoint_runs_as_least_privileged_user false), granting the elevation needed to access LSASS, the SAM, and cached secrets (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the local Administrators group and confirm only authorized admin/service accounts are members.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only authorized admin/service accounts listed (secure); the everyday interactive user present (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege; CIS Controls v8 Control 5/6

how_to_obtain.instruction: On macOS, read the admin group membership and confirm the daily user is not a member.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: macOS: only authorized admins in the admin group (secure); standard daily user present (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege

option_description: Device/identity sign-in and resource access enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn, Windows Hello for Business, or certificate) rather than password-only or phishable OTP/push.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Local credential theft and reuse" — fires when password-only/phishable auth is used (phishing_resistant_mfa_enabled false), so stolen endpoint credentials can be replayed to move laterally (ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Conditional Access / login policy to confirm phishing-resistant authenticators are enforced for device and resource access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Login policy shows phishing-resistant authenticators (FIDO2/WHfB/cert) enforced (secure); password-only or SMS/push (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet; NIST SP 800-63B

option_description: Full-disk encryption is on and complete for the system volume (BitLocker: VolumeStatus=FullyEncrypted, ProtectionStatus=On, EncryptionPercentage=100; FileVault: 'FileVault is On.').
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Lost or stolen device data exposure" — fires when the disk is unencrypted or the protector is suspended (endpoint_full_disk_encryption_on false), leaving local data and cached credentials readable to an offline attacker (ATT&CK T1052).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, read the BitLocker volume status for the system volume.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VolumeStatus=FullyEncrypted, ProtectionStatus=On, EncryptionPercentage=100 (secure). FullyDecrypted / ProtectionStatus=Off (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Get-BitLockerVolume (BitLocker) Microsoft Learn

how_to_obtain.instruction: On macOS, read FileVault status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "FileVault is On." (secure) or "FileVault is Off." (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Managing macOS FileVault 2 with fdesetup (Der Flounder); Apple fdesetup

option_description: A TPM is present and ready (TpmPresent=True and TpmReady=True via Get-Tpm, TPM 2.0 expected) to anchor boot/credential integrity and the disk-encryption key.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of both "Lost or stolen device data exposure" and "Boot-level persistence / firmware bootkit" — fires when no ready TPM is available (tpm_present_and_ready false), so the encryption key is more readily extractable offline and boot integrity is not hardware-anchored.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read TPM presence and readiness via Get-Tpm (TPM 2.0 expected); where disk encryption is in use also confirm the BitLocker KeyProtector includes Tpm.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TpmPresent : True and TpmReady : True (secure). TpmPresent : False (insecure / unsupported).
how_to_obtain.source: Confirm-SecureBootUEFI / TPM guidance, Microsoft Learn (tpm.msc, Get-Tpm)

option_description: Inactivity timeout in minutes after which the device automatically locks and requires a password/biometric to wake.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Lost or stolen device data exposure" — fires when the timeout exceeds 15 minutes, widening the window during which a lost or unattended device exposes an unlocked, decrypted session.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the machine-inactivity / require-password-after-screen-saver setting and confirm a short timeout with password required on wake.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Windows: Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options / GPO 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit'. macOS: System Settings > Lock Screen + 'Require password after screen saver begins'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Inactivity timeout set short (<= 15 min) and password required on wake (secure); disabled or very long (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

option_description: The organization can remotely lock/wipe this endpoint via MDM/UEM (an available, tested Wipe/Retire/Lock action in the MDM console).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Lost or stolen device data exposure" — fires when there is no remote-wipe capability (remote_wipe_enabled false), so a lost or stolen device cannot be remediated, prolonging exposure of local data and cached credentials (NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a Wipe/Retire/Lock action is available (and tested) for the device in the MDM/UEM console.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MDM console shows the device with available Wipe/Retire/Lock actions (secure); device not actionable (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise

option_description: UEFI Secure Boot is enabled so only signed bootloaders/firmware run, preventing boot-level persistence and bootkits (verified via Confirm-SecureBootUEFI).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Boot-level persistence / firmware bootkit" — fires when Secure Boot is disabled (secure_boot_enabled false), leaving the boot chain open to unsigned/tampered boot components (ATT&CK T1547).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm UEFI Secure Boot state via PowerShell (or the firmware/UEFI Secure Boot setting).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: True (Secure Boot enabled, secure). False (disabled, insecure). Error if BIOS/non-UEFI.
how_to_obtain.source: Confirm-SecureBootUEFI (SecureBoot) Microsoft Learn

option_description: The endpoint is enrolled and compliant in the org MDM/UEM (Intune/Jamf) so policy, patch, and configuration are centrally enforced and remote wipe is possible.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Unmanaged / unmonitored endpoint with network exposure" — fires when the device is unenrolled/unmanaged/non-compliant (managed_device_enrollment_enforced false), escaping central control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the device is Azure AD joined and MDM-enrolled on Windows (or check macOS enrollment).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Windows: AzureAdJoined : YES and MDM enrollment URLs present (secure); not joined / not enrolled (insecure). macOS: 'profiles status -type enrollment'.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise

option_description: Endpoint security/EDR alerts and OS security logs are forwarded to a central SIEM/EDR cloud so detections and incident evidence survive a compromised host.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Unmanaged / unmonitored endpoint with network exposure" — fires when logs are local-only or forwarding is broken (endpoint_audit_logs_centralised false), so a compromise goes undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the endpoint appears as an active/reporting sensor in the EDR/SIEM console with recent events.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Endpoint appears as an active/reporting sensor with recent events (secure); host missing or stale (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 — Audit Log Management; CIS Control 13 — Network Monitoring and Defense

option_description: The host-based firewall is enabled on ALL profiles (Domain/Private/Public) to limit inbound exposure and lateral movement.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Unmanaged / unmonitored endpoint with network exposure" — fires when any profile is disabled (host_firewall_enabled false), exposing inbound surface and lateral-movement opportunity.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, read the firewall profile state for all three profiles.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled : True for Domain, Private, and Public profiles (secure). Any False (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

how_to_obtain.instruction: On macOS, read the application-firewall global state.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: macOS: "Firewall is enabled. (State = 1)" (secure); State = 0 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

option_description: Off-network access to corporate systems is enforced through VPN/ZTNA with device-compliance/posture gating rather than direct internet exposure.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of the exposure "Unmanaged / unmonitored endpoint with network exposure" — fires when there is direct internet exposure or no posture check (vpn_ztna_posture_gating_enabled false), giving off-network exposure of corporate resources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm remote access to corporate resources is enforced via VPN/ZTNA with a device-posture/compliance policy in the access-broker/VPN/ZTNA console.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote access enforced via VPN/ZTNA with device posture (secure); split/no enforcement (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 — Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security
